Hand-to-Hand Capacitance in the Two-in-Hand PF Winding

§1 — The capacitances follow the conductor, not the insulation

The turn-resolved PF winding (coil_windings.turn_resolved_coil) places every turn physically through pf_turn_layout, in two readings of the two conductors wound in hand. In the separate reading each pancake is its own conductor length. In the interleaved reading, the main arm every PF study runs, the two conductors are wound side by side through both pancakes of a double pancake and joined at the outer joint. But turn_capacitances places the turn-insulation capacitance between each turn and the next one along the conductor, the edge list (i, i + 1) for every turn, in both readings. It lumps the pancake insulation as a single turn-pair capacitance at the middle of each double pancake.

In the separate reading, consecutive turns along the conductor are radial neighbours, so the chain is right. In the interleaved reading it is not. Consecutive turns of one conductor sit two positions apart, with a turn of the other conductor between them. Each turn is coupled to a turn the insulation does not separate it from, and the side-by-side turns of the two conductors carry no capacitance at all, except the pair at the joint. TurnLayout.neighbour_pairs records those side-by-side pairs, but only so the voltage between them can be read; no capacitance is placed on them.

That hand-to-hand capacitance is the strongest capacitive path in an interleaved winding. It sets how a fast edge or a converter line divides between the two conductors. That division is what the quench-detection bridge compares (quench-detection-converter-pickup §2), so the bridge cannot be built until it is right. It also moves every result taken on the main arm: the winding modes and their damping, the exterior-turn and section voltages, the PF frequency-response prediction, and the switched windows. This plan places the capacitances by the insulation (§2), measures how far each published result moves (§3), and republishes those that move beyond tolerance (§4).

§2 — Place each capacitance between the turns the insulation separates

In coil_windings.turn_capacitances, build the capacitance edges from each turn's placement, its unit, layer and radial_index from pf_turn_layout, never from its electrical order, in both readings:

  • Turn insulation (PF_TURN_INSULATION_M) joins each pair of radial neighbours in one pancake, at the existing cylindrical pair capacitance (turn_pair_capacitance).
  • Pancake insulation (PF_PANCAKE_INSULATION_M) joins each turn to the turn facing it in the other pancake of its double pancake. Its value is the facing annulus, ε0εr times 2πr times the radial pitch, over the gap. That face rule is written inline in turn_ground_capacitance today; expose it once and use it in both places rather than writing a second copy. This replaces the single lumped pair per double pancake.
  • A capacitance between two turns is split half between their start nodes and half between their end nodes. For two turns consecutive along the conductor this is the existing series chain.
  • No capacitance is placed between neighbouring double pancakes, as today. The record says so: IDM's inter-pancake insulation is not in the model.
  • The sectioned PF winding lumps this same turn network onto its sections (build_winding through coarse_capacitances). Today that lumping keeps a non-chain edge only when its two nodes fall in different groups, and silently drops one whose nodes fall in the same group. In the interleaved reading every hand-to-hand edge is such an edge. Carry it instead, by the energy it stores under a linear voltage across its section: an edge spanning Δ of a section's n turns adds C(Δ/n)2 to that section's series capacitance. The chain's existing series rule is unchanged.

Done when the following controls pass and the record gives PF6's terminal capacitance and its three lowest winding modes on the main arm, before and after. The record is docs/research/iter-two-in-hand-capacitance-census.html: this section opens it with PF6, and §3 extends it to every caller. Controls:

  • Arm invariance: map every edge to the physical positions of the two turns it joins. The two readings give the same set of position pairs and the same total capacitance, because they share one placement.
  • Separate reading: inside each pancake the radial edges reproduce today's chain to rounding. The first and last link of each pancake carry half, because the run of radial neighbours ends there: at the joint the next turn faces across pancake insulation, and between double pancakes no capacitance is placed. The record lists the number of such links, four per double pancake.
  • Interleaved reading: every neighbour_pairs entry carries a turn-insulation capacitance, and no two turns more than one radial position apart in one pancake are joined.
  • Negative control: today's electrical-order edges fail the arm-invariance check for the interleaved reading.
  • Lumping: a turn network with one extra edge inside a section lumps to a larger series capacitance for that section than the same network without it, and an edge across sections still joins their boundary nodes.

Library src/power_convertor/coil_windings.py, tests tests/test_coil_windings.py.

§3 — How far each result on the main arm moves

Rerun the headline measure of every study that builds a PF winding, turn-resolved or sectioned: every caller of turn_resolved_coil, of pf_turn_layout, or of build_winding for a PF coil, since the sectioned PF winding lumps the same turn network. Run each measure three times, each in a scratch worktree: at the commit before §2's merge, at §2's merge, and at the head after §5's merge. The first step isolates the capacitance placement, the second the sectioning and lumping of §5, so every shift is attributed to the change that caused it. The callers include winding_damping (the modal quality factors), the PF2 and PF5 winding modes and their line amplification, frequency_response_prediction, exterior_turn_voltages, stray_sensitivity, section_step_convergence, switched_line_amplification, switched_discharge_insertion, pf_switched_pulse, the whole-pulse ripple's quench-detection table, and the figure scripts plant_section_gates and iter_sectioned_coil_terminal_impedance. The headline is the number each record states in its own summary.

Done when one table gives, for every caller found, the study, its record, the headline at each of the three revisions, each step's shift in percent, and whether the headline now crosses a reference it did not. A caller left out carries a stated reason. Negative control: a study that builds no PF turn model, the sectioned CS winding, shows no shift. A zero shift on a PF study is reported beside the count of capacitance edges its winding carries before and after, so that a dropped edge cannot read as a physical no-change. Caller scripts/iter/two_in_hand_capacitance_census.py, record docs/research/iter-two-in-hand-capacitance-census.html, which §2 opened.

§4 — Republish what moved

Rerun and republish each record whose headline moved more than 5 % in §3's table, or now crosses a reference it did not. Each record is updated in place with a dated note naming the capacitance placement, and its figures are redrawn, rendered and inspected. A record whose study belongs to a plan still in flight goes to that plan as a followup rather than being edited here. Each republished headline is re-measured at the current head, not copied from the census, because the census receipts carry no commit SHA.

§3's table selects these, republished here, one node per record family:

  • The PF2 and PF5 winding modes and their line amplification, including PF2's switched line gain, in the record of iter-pf-winding-line-resonance. The census read the switched-line amplifier's mode_hz (1,019, 736 and 3,000 Hz for PF2) as a mode it had selected against installed modes of 593, 519 and 521 Hz. But mode_hz is the retuning reference that pf_switched_pulse.retuned_winding scales the capacitances by. With it at the lossless ladder's first mode, the loaded arm is the winding as built and the detuned arm scales every capacitance by 1/1.32. So the loaded-to-detuned line gain is sound and needs no code change. The record reports PF2's installed first mode beside the gain, so the label is not mistaken for the mode the line meets.
  • PF6's installed damping, a driven-peak Q of 2.5 rising to 11.1, in the PF6 winding-damping record.
  • PF6's exterior hand peak, 4,965 V falling to 2,159 V, now below the 2.5 kV turn design reference, in the exterior-turn record.
  • PF6's terminal-impedance and sampled-impedance modes, the plant terminal peak and the initiation across-coil peak, in the frequency-response, plant-gate and initiation records, and the draft PF frequency-response measurement request.
  • The band factor at head, in two nodes once the impedance and line-resonance records have landed. The first node regenerates the canonical stores. The second restates the bands, and it spans both record families because one script, winding_damping.py, writes both of them. Each winding mode's band runs from the model value up to that value times the measured-to-model ratio of PF6's first tied mode. The measured end is YVUELA's sweep, at or above 2 kHz. scripts/iter/winding_damping.py reads the model end from data/iter/frequency_response_prediction/summary.json, and no republish has rewritten that store: the impedance republish wrote its head results to a study-local copy. So the damping and line-resonance band tables still use the pre-placement 1708.10 Hz and a factor of 1.1709. At head the tied mode is 1056.93 Hz and the factor is 1.8923, which puts PF5's 300 Hz line back inside its band (249.0–471.1 Hz). Regenerate the canonical frequency-response store at head and point the damping script's inputs back at canonical stores. Then restate the band tables, headlines and band figures of the damping and line-resonance records on the head factor, and re-pin the band tests. The placement moved PF6's model tied mode further from YVUELA's measurement, from 17 % to 89 % below it. The records say so, and the factor carries that widening into every band.
  • Last, the model claims register, once the records above are republished.

Each node re-pins the tests that pin its record's old values, and two that are physical criteria are restated rather than relaxed. These go to the plans that own them, as followups: PF6's stray-driven section swing (+314 %) to iter-switched-terminal-transients; PF1's insertion section peak (+18 %) to coil-circuit-playback-figures §8; the whole-pulse bridge table (+97 %) to quench-detection-converter-pickup §5; and the converter filter screen, if it moved, to coil-supply-report-rebuild §7.

Done when every row of §3's table beyond tolerance carries a republished record or a followup on its owning plan, and the eight tests left red by §2 are green or restated. The canonical frequency-response store gives PF6's first shorted resonance at its head value, 1056.93 Hz, rather than 1708.10 Hz. Every band in the damping and line-resonance records equals its model value times the factor that store implies. The census record's statement that the switched-line source selector needs repair carries a dated correction saying it does not. Negative control: a record within tolerance is left unchanged.

§5 — The sectioned PF winding at the resolution the hand capacitance needs

§2's placement leaves the sectioned PF winding unable to resolve what it now places. Each double pancake is one section, so both hands share its two nodes, and the capacitance between them can only be carried as stored energy. On PF6 the build at the layout count, nine sections, misses the turn-resolved modes by 9, 31 and 34 %, against 0.2, 4.7 and 12.7 % before §2. The converged count default_sections gives (SECTION_SPLIT: four per double pancake on PF1, PF3, PF5 and PF6, so 36 on PF6; 30 on PF2; 88 on PF4) agrees within 2.4 % on PF6 on the new network, while PF1 misses by 1.3, 6.0 and 6.8 % (§2's evidence); the other four coils are not yet measured. Those counts were set on the old network, where the family's note puts the converged agreement at 1, 5 and 5 %. Some callers pass it (pf_switched_pulse, section_step_convergence, plant_section_gates), but others build at the layout count: switched_discharge_insertion, switched_voltage_waveforms, initiation_transient, thyristor_voltage_steps, stray_sensitivity and scripts/iter/coil_windings.py. Three changes in coil_windings, and none in the callers:

  • build_winding builds a two-in-hand PF coil at default_sections when no section count is passed, so every PF caller resolves the hand capacitance. SECTION_SPLIT keeps its converged counts. CS, VS and JT-60SA windings keep their present default. This reverses, for two-in-hand PF coils only, the rule that a bare build takes its layout count and the converged count is requested, because the layout count no longer represents that winding. tests/test_coil_windings.py::test_the_default_build_keeps_the_geometry_count_and_the_converged_count_is_explicit pins the old rule; rewrite it to pin both halves, the two-in-hand PF default and every other coil's layout count.
  • Each PF coil's SECTION_SPLIT entry is re-derived on the new network: the smallest split, in steps of the present ones, at which the three lowest modes agree with the turn-resolved build within 5 %. PF2's third mode is excepted, because the note above SECTION_SPLIT says it settles away from the turn-resolved build however finely it is split. For PF2 that mode is held to its settled value as the done-when states, and the other two modes to the 5 %. PF1 is already measured to miss at its present split: 6.0 and 6.8 % on modes 2 and 3 at 32 sections, so it moves. The note above SECTION_SPLIT is rewritten to state the new counts and their agreement. The assertions in tests/test_coil_windings.py that pin the present counts (default_sections of PF1 and PF6, and any other) are updated to the re-derived counts, each with its old and new value in the record.
  • coarse_capacitances applies the series rule only to a group whose chain of node-adjacent links is complete. A group whose chain is broken, as it is in the interleaved reading everywhere but the joint, carries those links by the same stored-energy rule as its other edges.

Done when, for all six PF coils on the main arm, build_winding called with no section count gives three lowest modes within 5 % of the turn-resolved build, and the record gives each coil's section count and agreement. The exception is a mode that the convergence note above SECTION_SPLIT says settles away from the turn-resolved build however finely it is split: PF2's third mode, 6 % before §2. That mode is measured on the new network at splits of 5, 10 and 20. Split 20 is PF2's finest, one turn per section of its 120 turns, so its value is the settled one. The gate for it is that the chosen count lies within 1 % of the split-20 value, and the record states the settled shortfall against the turn-resolved build. The run time of one PF6 switched window at the new count is measured against the old and stated. Negative control: a group with one chain link missing gives a smaller series capacitance under the corrected rule than under the series rule. Library src/power_convertor/coil_windings.py, tests tests/test_coil_windings.py, record docs/research/iter-two-in-hand-capacitance-census.html.
